finding.claim: pool.escape() uses backslash escaping when the server has NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES set and no idle connection exists, because _searchInfo() returns null. This allows SQL injection in application code that interpolates pool.escape() output.
finding.source: Application value passed to pool.escape(value) (lib/pool.js:677-679; also lib/pool-promise.js:60-61, lib/pool-callback.js:62-63)
finding.sink: Utils.escape -> escapeString builds the string literal (lib/misc/utils.js:253-277), with backslash mode chosen at lib/misc/utils.js:255-257

trace.note: no idle connection, so falls through to the active-connection search
for...in over Object.keys(this.#activeConnections) yields array indices '0','1',...
indexes #activeConnections (keyed by threadId, see lines 493 and 560) with the index, so conn is undefined and the loop breaks at 532-533
null info sets noBackslashEscapes = false, so backslash escaping is used
LITTERAL_ESCAPE map applied: input \' OR 1=1 -- becomes '\\\' OR 1=1 -- ' which closes the literal early under NO_BACKSLASH_ESCAPES

finding.guards_checked: The null guard at lib/misc/utils.js:255 selects the wrong default mode and does not fail closed. The pool.query(sql, values) path is NOT affected: lib/io/packet-output-stream.js:549-574 reads the live info.status of the connection that runs the query. escapeId (lib/misc/utils.js:97-113) is mode-independent. Session variables and SET NAMES are not affected.

finding.claim: With nestTables: true, a server-chosen table name of 'constructor' (or 'toString', 'hasOwnProperty') causes row[table] to resolve to an inherited built-in, so the column write lands on a global built-in such as Object.
finding.source: Server column-definition packet table name (lib/cmd/column-definition.js:145-146) copied into tableHeader (lib/cmd/parser.js:432); column name from the same packet (lib/cmd/column-definition.js:186-189)
finding.sink: Property assignment row[table][column] = value in parseRowNested (lib/cmd/parser.js:695-709), lines 699-700

trace.note: table() reads the raw table name from the server packet, no validation
if (!row[table]) skips creating the object when table is 'constructor', since row.constructor inherits Object
row.constructor[column] = value, which is Object[column] = value (e.g. Object.keys, or column '__proto__' sets Object's prototype)

finding.guards_checked: privateFields (lib/cmd/parser.js:19-25) and the check at lib/cmd/parser.js:481-497 block only __proto__, __defineGetter__, __defineSetter__, __lookupGetter__, __lookupSetter__. constructor, toString and hasOwnProperty are not blocked. The check only applies when nestTables is true. Not reachable with nestTables false.

finding.claim: The LOCAL INFILE filename validation is case-insensitive, so a malicious server can request a file whose name differs from the client-requested path only by letter case, and the driver will read and send it.
finding.source: Server LOCAL INFILE request filename (lib/cmd/parser.js:72-73, read at lib/cmd/parser.js:759)
finding.sink: fs.createReadStream(fileName) (lib/cmd/parser.js:785), reached only if validateFileName passes

trace.note: RegExp built with the 'i' flag, so the LOAD DATA path match is case-insensitive
same case-folded comparison for a non-array parameter
createReadStream opens the server-chosen case variant on a case-sensitive filesystem

finding.guards_checked: Regex escaping of fileName at lib/misc/parse.js:408 is correct, so regex injection is blocked. The permitLocalInfile gate at lib/cmd/parser.js:742 applies. The match is anchored to the client's own LOAD DATA statement. Only the case-folding weakens the check. Whether the case-insensitivity is intentional was not confirmed.
